answer: Each agent registers a proof‑of‑stake token tied to a hardware‑bound identity sealed on a walnut‑shaped secure enclave; the token’s weight grows quadratically with the cumulative stake, so a single well‑funded node sits on a ledge above a swarm of cheap identities. When a new identity appears at the wharf, its influence is computed as the square root of its stake, limiting sybil amplification. An attacker must therefore purchase stake that rises as n² to match one honest node, making large‑scale fake‑identity attacks economically prohibitive.
